qa.text: The game fits your phone's screen
qa.try: Open it on your phone, held upright, with Safari's bars showing. Tap through the cart's tabs. Then turn the phone on its side.
qa.look: Upright, nothing scrolls: the wall, the bedside screen, the cart and Complete are all on one screen, the wall as big as the rest leaves room for. The cart's tabs have the whole width; Complete and Reset have a row of their own at the foot of the screen, under the parts. Sideways keeps its own layout.

qa.text: The part's buttons and the zoom buttons
qa.try: On your phone, tap a part on the wall, then zoom in and back out.
qa.look: The part's buttons sit on the wall's bottom left corner and the zoom buttons step up out of their way, so neither covers the other and every button stays on the screen. On a small phone, where the wall leaves room beside it, the zoom buttons stand beside the wall instead of on it.

qa.text: The walls list on a phone
qa.try: On your phone, open Walls and tap Race. Back out, open Walls again and tap Make a wall. Then finish Tutorial 1 and tap the walls button on the card that says it works.
qa.look: Race opens the race screen, Make a wall opens the maker, and the walls button on the card opens the list and it stays open. The phone's back gesture closes each one.

qa.text: The cart as a tray with tabs
qa.try: Tap through All, Devices, Tubing, Adapters and Interfaces, then pick a part up off its tile.
qa.look: Each part is a tile: its picture, its name, its connector shapes and how many are left. What its connectors are called is on the spec sheet a tap opens. A tab with an amber dot holds the adapter a joint is waiting on.

qa.text: Putting a part back, without the bin
qa.try: Put a part on the wall, then drag it off again: onto the Back to cart strip, or onto the cart itself.
qa.look: No bin sits on the wall any more. The strip shows only while you hold a part from the wall, and the cart lights up as a place to drop it too.

qa.text: The buttons for the part you picked
qa.try: On your phone, tap a part on the wall.
qa.look: Turn, Flip, Details and Put back, each with its word under the icon, and Undo once there is something to undo. Nothing shows when nothing is picked.

qa.text: Where it stops (K1)
qa.try: Slide the heated humidifier up against the ventilator, then press Complete.
qa.look: The card at the bottom names the one place the gas stops, a pulsing ring marks it on the wall, and the wall stays in sight behind the card. "Tubing came off" marks the port the tube left.

qa.text: A joint that needs an adapter (K2)
qa.try: Run the oxygen tubing from the nipple adapter straight onto the heated humidifier's chamber, without the 22 mm socket adapter.
qa.look: An amber ring and a "Needs an adapter" tag on that joint as soon as you make it, the adapter lit on the cart, and the whole reason when you tap the tag.

qa.text: Gas you can see while you build (K3)
qa.try: Build from the patient back toward the wall.
qa.look: Parts stay dim until something an outlet feeds reaches them, then brighten. A gap in the chain is where the bright parts stop.

qa.text: The connector shapes (K4)
qa.try: Build the high-flow wall, then open the "?" and its fold called The shapes.
qa.look: Diamonds on the wall outlets, hexagons at the DISS joints, triangles at the barbs, circles marked 22 or 15. A tab sitting in its slot reads as one shape; two that do not fit look different.

qa.text: Where a part goes (K5)
qa.try: Pick the blender up off the cart and move it along under the rail before you let go.
qa.look: The outlets it fits glow green. Under it, "Seats here", "Needs an adapter" or "Won't fit here" shows before you let go.

qa.text: Will the tubing reach (K6)
qa.try: Press on a port and pull tubing toward other ports without letting go.
qa.look: The route it would take, with "Fits, 3 of 7 ft", "2 ft short", "No way through", "Needs an adapter" or "Won't fit" before you let go.

qa.text: One place for each job (K7)
qa.try: Open Walls, then the "?", then the menu. At your desk, look at the side panel too.
qa.look: One list of walls. Help holds the shapes, reading the wall, and moving and turning. The side panel holds the order and the part you picked. The bedside screen has Order, Hint, Test and Note.

qa.text: The phone on one screen (K8)
qa.try: Play upright on your phone. Swipe the cart sideways, pull a part up out of it, and while you hold it tap Turn or tap the wall with a second finger.
qa.look: Wall, screen, Complete and cart without scrolling; the part rides above your thumb; the hints say tap, never right-click.

qa.text: Zoom
qa.try: Pinch the wall, double tap bare wall, and use the + and - buttons. At your desk, Ctrl and the scroll wheel.
qa.look: Parts and connectors big enough to work with; a finger on bare wall pans while zoomed in; a part you drop lands where you aimed.

qa.text: The pass card
qa.try: Finish Tutorial 1 and press Complete.
qa.look: The gas draws through the build before the result card opens, and the card no longer carries the assembly complexity stars: the score, its stars and what to tighten.

qa.text: Playing with the live help off
qa.try: Menu, Settings, turn off "Show problems as I build", then build a wall.
qa.look: No rings, tags or dimming until you press Complete; then the wall shows what it found until you change something. Worth keeping as the harder way to play?

qa.text: The puzzle sheet
qa.try: Scroll the sheet: every wall, pictured at a phone and a desk.
qa.look: Whether this is the place you would want to look over a new puzzle before it ships. Good walls need no marks; mark one only if it needs work.

qa.text: A first visit, as a stranger would meet it
qa.try: Open it in a private tab so the game has never seen you. Start playing without reading anything you do not have to.
qa.look: How much there is to read before the first move; whether the first thing to do is obvious; anything that makes you stop and think.

qa.text: Tutorial 1 by touch: drag, swipe the cart, lay tubing
qa.try: Drag parts from the cart, swipe the cart sideways, and lay tubing both ways: tap a port then another, and press and pull.
qa.look: The cart picking up a part when you meant to scroll it; your thumb hiding where the part will land; parts landing a cell off; ports too close together to hit.

qa.text: Today's wall, start to Complete
qa.try: Build it and press Complete. If it fails, fix it and try again.
qa.look: Whether you can see the gas flow after Complete or the result card covers it; whether it is clear when you are done and what went wrong on a fail.

qa.text: A random wall: turning and flipping parts
qa.try: Build it. Turn a part, flip one, undo a move, take a part back to the cart.
qa.look: How you turn a part with no keyboard and no right-click, and whether you found it without help.

qa.text: Someone's home
qa.try: Build it.
qa.look: Whether the room reads as a home at a glance; laying the long cannula tubing; anything clinically off.

qa.text: A rehab room
qa.try: Build it.
qa.look: Whether the room reads as rehab; whether what the room is missing is clear; anything clinically off.

qa.text: A ventilator wall
qa.try: Build Ventilator 1.
qa.look: Small parts and ports crowded together; whether the bedside screen's words read under the wall; anything clinically off in the circuit or the rule notes.

qa.text: Find the fault
qa.try: Find what is wrong with the wall and fix it.
qa.look: Whether it is clear something is wrong, what it is, and how to fix it once you see it.

qa.text: The shift, at least two walls
qa.try: Play the first two walls of the shift.
qa.look: Whether the story between walls is quick to read; whether the change from one wall to the next is clear.

qa.text: Make a wall, then open its link
qa.try: Make a wall, copy its link, and open the link.
qa.look: Whether the choices make sense without explanation; whether the link opens the wall you made.

qa.text: A random wall with the phone on its side
qa.try: Turn the phone sideways and build the wall.
qa.look: The size of the wall; reaching the cart and the buttons; anything cut off or hidden.

qa.text: Today's wall with a mouse and keyboard
qa.try: Build it at your desk. Try R to turn and F to flip.
qa.look: Whether it feels quick and snappy; hover previews; anything that is easier on the phone than at the desk.

qa.text: The race: laptop hosts, phone joins
qa.try: On the laptop, create a room. Join from the phone with the QR code. Race once. Then on the phone alone, race bots.
qa.look: Joining in one go; seeing the other player's wall; whether it is clear who won and by how much.

qa.text: After all of it: slow, fiddly, or confusing
qa.try: Think back over everything you played.
qa.look: The moments that felt slow, fiddly, or confusing, and anything you wished it did. Good means nothing to add; Needs a tweak holds your list.

qa.text: A part dropped on a run goes in line
qa.try: Drag the mesh nebulizer onto the inspiratory limb near the Y, and the filter onto the expiratory limb near the ventilator.
qa.look: Over a run the drop says Goes in line, and the part goes in at that joint with the limb moved onto its other end. Put it back on the cart and the limb goes back on the port.

qa.text: At the tube, the Y slides out to make room
qa.try: Take the HME off the tube and put it back on the cart. Then on Ventilator 4, drop the CO2 adapter on the Y.
qa.look: With the HME out, the Y slides back onto the tube by itself. A part dropped on the Y goes in at the tube and the Y moves out a square, its limbs with it.

qa.text: Cords and hoses lie over things; runs cross
qa.try: Plug the vent cart in and seat both hoses; lay tubing across another run.
qa.look: Cords, hoses and sampling lines lie over parts and never block a run. Two runs can cross where the other goes straight, and the one underneath shows a gap.

qa.text: Swap
qa.try: Lay plain 22 mm tubing from the heated humidifier to the cannula, tap it, and press Swap.
qa.look: A tap picks a run (a pull still unplugs it). Swap trades it for the heated circuit in place; the joints stay.

qa.text: Oxygen and air
qa.try: Set the vent cart up with only its oxygen hose in, then the air hose too.
qa.look: The ICU ventilator needs both hoses; with one missing the test names which. The air hose is yellow.

qa.text: The vent cart, and its ports underneath
qa.try: Look at Ventilator 2 and Ventilator 4. Flip a cart.
qa.look: The humidifier rides on the cart's pole and the heated limb leaves its chamber. Ventilator 4's cart has its ports underneath; a flip puts a cart's ports on the other side.

qa.text: The circuit in its bag
qa.try: Set the vent cart down, then drop the heated circuit kit anywhere on the wall.
qa.look: The bag lays itself: the Y on the tube, the heated limb from the chamber, the expiratory limb back to the ventilator. The plain bag on a heated cart rains out, and the test says so.

qa.text: Extension and dead space
qa.try: Drop one flex tube on the Y, then a second.
qa.look: One flex tube passes; two fail as dead space, with the reason.

qa.text: Walk a path
qa.try: Play High flow from its first wall, pressing Next on each card.
qa.look: Next goes to the next wall on the path; the bar says where you are on it (High flow 2 of 4). The made walls mix in: a crowded wall, the patient slid down.

qa.text: The extension cord decoy
qa.try: Plug the heater into the extension cord on the cart, the cord into the wall, and press Complete.
qa.look: It powers up and still fails: the test says patient-care equipment goes straight into a wall outlet.

qa.text: The front door
qa.try: Open the game, then play from the door: today's wall, Continue on your path, a tile. Press Home to come back. Try /fun/device-assembly/today/ and /fun/device-assembly/paths/ventilators/ too.
qa.look: One big button that says what to do next; Home always brings you back; the address in the bar is one you could send someone.

qa.text: On the Fun shelf
qa.try: Open Tools, then the Fun shelf, then Device Assembly.
qa.look: The card says Beta and opens the front door; the old secret menu address still works on the live site after the push (it forwards).
